gaps: No Korean cuisine at all despite the cook having a carbon steel wok and high-heat capability.
No Japanese cuisine despite a clear interest in Asian cooking and noodles.
No seafood protein of any kind.
North Indian cooking is absent — the one Indian dish is South Indian (kanji).
No West African or sub-Saharan African cuisine.
Tofu has never appeared as a protein despite a vegetarian adult and a wok.
Weekend project dishes are almost entirely missing — nearly every dish is a weeknight one-pot.
Fish is a completely untapped protein that works quickly on a weeknight.

ideas.title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice with Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens Korean cuisine entirely — zero Korean dishes in the collection — and the beef is a straightforward skip for the vegetarian adult since the vegetables carry the dish.

ideas.title: Dal Tadka (Restaurant-Style)
ideas.why: Fills the North Indian gap — the only Indian dish they have is South Indian — and introduces the tadka technique (blooming spices in ghee) which is absent from the whole collection.

ideas.title: Vegan Mapo Tofu
ideas.why: Puts the carbon steel wok to real Sichuan use and introduces tofu as a protein — a complete blank in the collection — while being as-written vegan so the whole table eats the same bowl.

ideas.title: Marinated Fish Tacos
ideas.why: Fish is the only mainstream protein entirely absent from the collection, and this slots into the taco format the family already enjoys without any pantry leap.

ideas.title: West African Chicken Peanut Stew (Groundnut Stew)
ideas.why: West African cuisine is a total blank in the collection and this one-pot braise uses pantry staples (peanut butter, tomatoes, chicken) so the barrier is low despite the new flavour territory.

ideas.title: Miso Tori Paitan Ramen (Creamy Chicken Broth Ramen)
ideas.why: Japanese cuisine is absent from the collection and this is the kind of ambitious weekend project — building a proper paitan broth, tare, and aroma oil from scratch — that a cook with this equipment clearly has the skills and appetite for.
